release_notes:
The first firmware release since the ArkLights app went live on the App Store
and Google Play. Two and a half months of work: motion, safety, updates, and a
lot of hardening.

### Motion and lighting

- **Rebuilt the motion pipeline.** Gravity and rider-motion are now separated
  before any decision is made, which is what direction detection, braking and
  blinkers all depend on. Previously they shared one noisy signal and the
  thresholds fought each other.
- **Mount-aware orientation.** The board works out how it is mounted and
  interprets lean and turn relative to that, instead of assuming one fixed
  orientation.
- **Center Hold.** Hold the middle section of a linear strip on a solid colour
  while the edges keep running the effect. Per strip, configurable width.
- **Lean glow tuning** exposed as live settings rather than compiled-in numbers.

### Safety and recovery

- **Low-battery detection.** A pack that collapses under LED load now parks the
  board in a dim red blink and holds there, instead of silently rebooting in a
  loop. Recovers on a power cycle with a healthy pack.
- **Recovery mode is visible and reachable.** Slow amber breathing means the
  board restarted into recovery after repeated crashes — it is not bricked. Its
  Wi-Fi network is suffixed `-R` so you can tell it apart, and the recovery
  server no longer depends on the LED driver, so it still comes up when the LED
  subsystem is the thing that crashed.
- **Crash diagnostics.** The board records why it last reset and shows it,
  rather than leaving you guessing between a crash, a brownout and a power cut.
- **LED power budgeting** so a strip at full white cannot pull the supply down.

### Updates

- **Firmware updates are ~3x faster over Bluetooth** and no longer stall
  mid-transfer. The old update path erased flash in blocks as it went, freezing
  both cores for ~150ms at a time; it now erases once up front and streams.
- **A progress bar on the strip itself** while updating, so you can watch it
  from the board rather than the phone.
- **Updates are verified before they are booted.** A truncated or corrupt image
  is rejected rather than flashed.

### Group sync

- **Headlight sync opt-out** — keep taillights synced across a group while each
  board keeps its own headlight.
- **Direction handling fixed on single-strip installs**, where the taillight is
  a section of one continuous strip rather than a separate strip.
- **Group membership survives a firmware update** instead of quietly resetting.

### Security

- Destructive actions (firmware updates, factory reset, changing the access
  point password) now require proving you know the board's password.
- Optional 4-digit connection PIN, off by default.
- Fixed the settings endpoint returning the access point password and PIN to
  anyone who asked.
- Fixed a bug where applying Wi-Fi settings rebooted the board before saving
  them, losing the new password every time.

### Housekeeping

- Automated test suite (42 tests) covering the Bluetooth frame codec and the
  boot/recovery decision logic, run on every change.
- Build-time guard that fails if a firmware image outgrows its update slot.
- Third-party attributions (`NOTICE`) now ship with every release.
